what_it_is: A ~0.99 m flexible rope lying on the table, clamped at (0.05, 0) (marker 1), its free end held by the tool (marker 20); 20 markers ~0.052 m apart. Task = cable routing: drag the rope through three pegs so it wraps each on the required side, and park the end at the target. 'load' = magnitude of the force the rope exerts on the tool; it is a dynamic force (drag + inertia of the sliding rope, rubbing on pegs, and a small elastic part from bent rope), not a static tension.

mechanisms.name: inextensible-ish chain clamped at marker 1, end on the tool
mechanisms.evidence: marker 1 std 0 over 200 snapshots and all logs; |marker20-tool| < 2e-6; polyline 0.988..1.000 m in all logs incl. life_1 near-taut pull

mechanisms.name: viscous table drag + rope inertia (superlinear 'fights back when you hurry')
mechanisms.evidence: life_1 speed steps on the same rope: load 0.45/0.7/1.7/3.4/6.0 N at 0.02/0.05/0.10/0.15/0.20 m/s; Coulomb part fitted ~0 (fc=0.002 N)
mechanisms.confidence: high for the speed dependence in the dragging regime; individual m/cv values are effective (coarse chain)

mechanisms.name: rope pushes back (bilateral links) and bending elasticity
mechanisms.evidence: life_1 t=236-244: pushing slack rope back at 0.3 m/s -> 4.3 N; at rest the coiled rope creeps (sum|v| ~0.1 m/s) with load 0.45 N, straight rope at rest 0.13-0.19 N (life_1 t>430)
mechanisms.confidence: medium (world predicts 2.2 N for the 4.3 N push peak)

mechanisms.name: near-taut stiffening
mechanisms.evidence: life_1 t=400-426: at 0.06 m/s load 4.1 -> 9.0 N as end-to-end 0.91 -> 0.98 m; emerges from chain + drag (world 5.3 N at the last point: under-predicts the final rise)

mechanisms.name: rope rubbing on pegs (capstan-like)
mechanisms.evidence: observation logs: load/sum|v| 3.9 -> 5.2 -> 6.1 for wrap 0-1, 1-2, 2-3 rad; fitted extra tangential drag of touching nodes

mechanisms.name: tool servo: reference ramps to the command at 0.30 m/s, force-limited PD, tool mass, peg blocks the tool
mechanisms.evidence: life_1: tool_vel reading 0.011/0.030/0.068/0.115/0.172 vs displacement speed 0.02/0.05/0.10/0.15/0.20 (reference reaches each command early in the step, then waits); 906/908: tool held at 0.045 from a peg, lag up to 0.094 m, then lurch 0.3-0.74 m/s -> overload
mechanisms.confidence: high for tracking, medium for the snag/lurch magnitude (world under-predicts the 908 spike: 6.9 vs 11.2 N)

mechanisms.name: load read-out
mechanisms.evidence: fitted jointly; mean |error| 0.44 N on fit segments

different_from_hypothesis: Hypothesis: load ~ c * sum|v_i| (linear friction). Found: strongly superlinear in drag speed (life_1), best explained with inertia + viscous drag; Coulomb friction ~0.
Hypothesis: load = rope tension. Found: the rope also pushes on the tool (slack push gives 4 N), so load is the magnitude of the rope force, tension or compression.
Hypothesis: reset load 0.23-0.85 N unexplained offset. Found: the coiled rope keeps relaxing (markers creep at rest), i.e. a bending-elastic force; a straight rope at rest reads ~0.15 N.

Hypothesis assumed a taut rope gives a large static tension. Not observed: at end-to-end 0.983 m (rope 0.994 m) the rope at rest reads 0.18 N; only pulling it near taut raises the load steeply (dynamic).

World artefact found during design: in a few simulated situations (seed 12) the chain gets stretched between two pegs and holds ~9 N at rest; the real rope did not (life_3 max 4.1 N). The controller has a back-off guard for it.
field_note_refers_to: 'Fights back when you hurry': the rope's resisting force grows faster than linearly with drag speed (x13 from 0.02 to 0.20 m/s on the same rope), so the old program's fixed 0.15 m/s overloads once ~15 nodes slide and wrap pegs; and if the tool is held by a peg, the servo catches up at up to 0.3-0.7 m/s and the load spikes (906: 21 N).

lives.life_1: seed 18, scripted probe: speed steps, lateral drag, slack fast push, near-taut pull (600 steps, no overload, max 9.97 N)
lives.life_2: seed 3, controller end-to-end: success at step 378, max load 4.63 N (world: success 388, 5.35 N)
lives.life_3: seed 12 (world's hardest case), controller: success at step 308, max load 4.13 N (world: success 328, 9.71 N)
